'''Paul Frederick Zweifel''' (June 21, 1929 – February 12, 2017) was a [[Mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] and a prominent leader in the mathematical theory of [[Nuclear reactor|nuclear reactors]] and the mathematical development of [[linear transport theory]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=McCormick |first1=Norman J. |last2=Siewert |first2=Charles E. |last3=Ganapol |first3=Barry D. |last4=Prinja |first4=Anil K. |date=2017-08-01 |title=Paul Frederick Zweifel |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/70/8/73/939850/Paul-Frederick-Zweifel |journal=Physics Today |language=en |volume=70 |issue=8 |pages=73 |doi=10.1063/PT.3.3671 |bibcode=2017PhT....70h..73M |issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription }}</ref> a discipline that encompasses [[neutron transport]] in the core of a nuclear reactor as well as the propagation of photons in [[radiative transfer]].

In transport theory, he pioneered the use of rigorous mathematics for analytically solving the linear transport equation. He developed existence and uniqueness theorems for the neutron transport equation and investigated the spectrum of the linear transport operator under general conditions.<ref name=":0" />

== Early years ==
Paul Zweifel was born on June 21, 1929, in [[New York City]], to Dorothy and Frederick Zweifel. His family moved to [[Spartanburg, South Carolina|Spartanburg]], [[South Carolina]]. When he was fifteen, he received the Pepsi-Cola Scholarship to attend the college of his choice, Carnegie Institute of Technology (now [[Carnegie Mellon University]]),<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-02-15 |title=Zweifel, Paul Frederick |url=https://roanoke.com/obituaries/zweifel-paul-frederick/article_28b120a1-0370-5d7a-94cf-db98ac9ed5e8.html |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=Roanoke Times |language=en}}</ref> and graduated with a B.S. in Physics in 1948.<ref name=":3" /> 

He received his Ph.D. in Physics in 1954 under the guidance of Eugene Greuling at [[Duke University]].<ref name=":0" />The title of his dissertation was ''Capture-Positron Branching Ratios''. He was in the lineage of Ph.D. dissertation advisors, starting with [[Josef Stefan]], [[Ludwig Boltzmann]], [[Paul Ehrenfest]], [[George Uhlenbeck]], [[Emil Konopinski]], E. Greuling, and P. F. Zweifel.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=McCormick |first1=Norman J. |last2=Garcia |first2=Roberto D. M. |last3=Siewert |first3=Charles E. |date=2018-04-16 |title=Biographical Memoir and Publications of Paul F. Zweifel |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/23324309.2018.1508474 |journal=Journal of Computational and Theoretical Transport |language=en |volume=47 |issue=1–3 |pages=187–208 |doi=10.1080/23324309.2018.1508474 |issn=2332-4309|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Zweifel worked at the [[Knolls Atomic Power Laboratory]] as a physicist and a manager of theoretical physics,<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last1=Greenberg |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BDEDCAAAQBAJ&dq=%22University+Distinguished+Professor+of+Physics+and+Nuclear+Engineering%22&pg=PA324 |title=Modern Mathematical Methods in Transport Theory |last2=Polewczak |date=2013-11-22 |publisher=Birkhäuser |isbn=978-3-0348-5675-1 |language=en}}</ref> where he did research on the theory of the slowing down and thermalization of neutrons from mid-1953 to 1958.<ref name=":0" />

In 1958, he was appointed associate professor of nuclear engineering at the [[University of Michigan]], and he was promoted to professor in 1960.<ref name=":1" /> He began working with [[Kenneth Case|Kenneth M. Case]], a physicist who made pioneering contributions to neutron transport theory during the [[Manhattan Project]]. They published a monograph, ''Linear Transport Theory'', in 1967 on the linear [[Boltzmann equation]].<ref name=":0" /> The mathematical approach of Case and Zweifel enables a more direct solution to problems of the type analyzed by [[Boris Davison]] in his monograph ''Neutron Transport Theory'' and that of [[Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar]] in his treatise ''Radiative Transfer''.<ref name=":0" />

In 1968, Paul became a Professor of Physics at [[Virginia Tech]] in Blacksburg, and three years later, he was appointed as University [[Distinguished professor|Distinguished Professor]], the highest distinction a professor can attain there.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Distinguished Professors |url=https://history.unirel.vt.edu/content/history_unirel_vt_edu/en/faculty_staff/distinguished_professors.html |access-date=2024-03-09 |website=history.unirel.vt.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Conferences ==
During a sabbatical year from the University of Michigan spent as a Visiting Professor at the [[Middle East Technical University]] in 1964–1965, Paul and physicist [[Erdal İnönü]] organized a two-week NATO Advanced Study Institute on Transport Theory held in [[Ankara]], Turkey.<ref name=":0" /> The conference featured six established senior faculty from the United States, Germany, and Yugoslavia and was attended by junior faculty and advanced graduate students who spoke about their dissertation projects. The proceedings, edited by the conference organizers, were published in ''Developments in Transport Theory''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lee |first=Clarence E. |date=March 1969 |title=Developments in Transport Theory |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.13182/NSE69-A20027 |journal=Nuclear Science and Engineering |language=en |volume=35 |issue=3 |pages=410 |doi=10.13182/NSE69-A20027 |bibcode=1969NSE....35..410L |issn=0029-5639|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1969, Paul, along with Robert Erdmann and Charles Siewert, founded a series of conferences that have become known as the International Conference on Transport Theory, or ICTT meetings.<ref name=":0" /> The conferences continue to bring together experts in mathematical and applied transport theory from all parts of the world.<ref name=":0" /> As of 2024, there have been 27 meetings—none affiliated with any professional society—that were held in the United States, Italy, China, Brazil, Sweden, Russia, England, Hungary and France; Paul hosted six of the conferences in Blacksburg. The journal Transport Theory and Statistical Physics, or TTSP, with Paul as its founding editor from 1971 until 1981, has published the proceedings of many ICTT meetings; the journal was re-titled in 2014 to the Journal of Computational and Theoretical Transport in recognition of the growing popularity of numerical methods in transport theory.<ref name=":3" /> 

== Publications ==
Paul Zweifel published in a variety of professional and nonprofessional fields, especially in reactor physics and [[neutron scattering]], transport theory, and statistical physics.<ref name=":3" />Although he began his career in the field of nuclear reactors, his interests evolved to mathematical physics in general. He also published a significant number of technical papers in other areas, especially on the [[Music theory|theory of music]].<ref name=":3" />

He was the Ph.D. advisor of [[Joel H. Ferziger]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joel Ferziger - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=103259 |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> whose dissertation was ''The Theory of Neutron Slowing Down in Nuclear Reactor''s. Later, the authors turned that into a book of the same title,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=John |last2=Koseff |first2=Jeffrey R. |last3=Leonard |first3=Anthony |last4=Street |first4=Robert L. |date=2005-06-01 |title=Joel Henry Ferziger |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1996487 |journal=Physics Today |volume=58 |issue=6 |pages=74–75 |doi=10.1063/1.1996487 |bibcode=2005PhT....58f..74K |issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and Paul wrote a textbook entitled ''Reactor Physics''.<ref name=":0" />

== Honors ==
In 1972, he received from the [[United States Department of Energy]] the [[Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-12-28 |title=Paul F. Zweifel, 1972 |url=https://science.osti.gov/lawrence/Award-Laureates/1970s/zweifel |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=science.osti.gov |publisher=United States Department of Energy |language=en-US}}</ref> In 1974, he received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|John Simon Guggenheim Foundation Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paul F. Zweifel |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/paul-f-zweifel/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation... |language=en}}</ref> He was a Fellow of the American Physical Society since 1963,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |access-date=2024-03-09 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> and had an obituary published in Physics Today.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=McCormick |first1=Norman J. |last2=Siewert |first2=Charles E. |last3=Ganapol |first3=Barry D. |last4=Prinja |first4=Anil K. |date=2017-08-01 |title=Paul Frederick Zweifel |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/70/8/73/939850/Paul-Frederick-Zweifel |journal=Physics Today |language=en |volume=70 |issue=8 |pages=73 |doi=10.1063/PT.3.3671 |bibcode=2017PhT....70h..73M |issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Later years ==
Paul Zweifel retired from Virginia Tech in 1996<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: Paul Zweifel of the Department of Physics, supporter of Moss Arts Center |url=https://news.vt.edu/content/news_vt_edu/en/articles/2017/02/Science-InMemorialPaulZweifel.html |access-date=2024-02-08 |website=news.vt.edu |language=en}}</ref> but continued to publish professionally until 2014.<ref name=":3" /> Because he studied music beginning when he was four years old, took voice lessons as a youngster, and later performed as a vocalist,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stories of Giving: Paul Zweifel |url=https://tickets.artscenter.vt.edu/online/default.asp?doWork::WScontent::loadArticle=Load&BOparam::WScontent::loadArticle::article_id=D4729DE0-C9C9-475A-9ADD-7B6B0BBE4F19 |access-date=2024-03-09 |website=tickets.artscenter.vt.edu}}</ref> he taught an opera course at [[Virginia Tech]] after his retirement. He also established a business specialized in creating supertitles for opera companies nationwide. He and his wife supported Virginia Tech’s Moss Arts Center and endowed a scholarship to enable music students to participate in summer music festivals and professional development workshops.<ref name=":5" />

He died on February 12, 2017, at the age of 87.<ref name=":5" />
